To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The pQCD based theoretical model for heavy flavor transport in QGP is able to simultaneously explain the observed $R_\mathrm{AA}$ and $v_{2}$ for heavy flavors at RHIC.

the heavy quarks are a useful tool for probing the properties of QGP, and the heavy quark transport coefficients evaluated within the pQDC framework are able to describe the experimental data on $R_{\rm AA}$ and $V_2^{HF}$.
The pQCD calculations of $R_{\AA}$ of heavy quarks in QGP are consistent with experimental measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the propagation and energy loss of heavy flavors in QGP.
the study of the transport coefficients of heavy quarks propagating in QGP.
the study of the propagation of heavy quarks in the Quark Gluonic Plasma (QGP) created in relativistic heavy ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the observed suppression and flow of heavy flavor hadrons in heavy ion collisions at RHIC and Lhc energies can be understood as a result of the propagation of the charm and bottom quark through the hot and dense matter formed in the collision.
the observed $v_2^{\mathrm{HF}}$ at RHIC is a strong indication that charm and bottom quark propagation through QGP is dominated by radiative processes.
the pQCD based calculations of heavy quark transport in QGP are in good agreement with the RHIC data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heavy quark energy loss is consistent with the observed suppression of heavy quarks at RHIC.
the pQCD calculations of the drag and diffusion coefficients for heavy quarks can reproduce the experimental data of heavy flavor meson suppression and elliptic flow at RHIC.
the heavy quark diffusion coefficient is about 1.0-2.0 times larger than the radiative energy loss coefficient, and that the heavy quarks lose their energy mainly through collisional process.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the observed suppression of non-photonic electron production at RHIC and Lhc is consistent with a scenario where the heavy quarks are produced in the initial stages of the collision and propagate through the QGP.
the heavy quark transport coefficients evaluated in the pQCD are sufficient to reproduce the experimental data on $R_{\rm AA}$ and $V_2$ for charm and bottom quark.
the $R_{\rm AA}$ and $R_{\text {AA}}$ of the heavy flavor non-photonic electron at RHIC and LHA are sensitive probes for the QGP medium properties.
